newsitem.title: USA: High MTBE, RFG price draws product to NY Harbor.
newsitem.headline: High MTBE, RFG price draws product to NY Harbor.

text.p: Reformulated gasoline and methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) imports into New York Harbor look set to rise in the next few weeks with product drawn in by the current high prices, traders said.
Also helping to bring imports to the region back to more typical levels after recent declines is the easing of a couple of supply disruption situations.
Reformulated gasoline futures in the New York Harbor have risen 15 percent in the past month, pushing August futures up above 64 cents a gallon on Friday.
MTBE prices in the Harbor moved up from 83.50 cents a gallon at end June to 102, and from 85 cents to 96.5 in Houston.
Shipments of RFG were seen coming from both Europe and U.S. Gulf refiners.
"There were about four or five ships fixed this week (from the Gulf to the Harbor), for both gasoline and MTBE, covering about a million barrels," said a Houston shipping broker.
An international products broker said ARCO Chemical on Friday morning fixed 270,000 barrels of MTBE for a transatlantic voyage.
The material is coming from ARCO's two European plants, its 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) Rotterdam facility and its 14,000 bpd Fos Sur Mer plant in France.
ARCO usually imports material from its European facilities but had stopped shipments during Rotterdam's six-week turnaround straddling June and July.

"ARCO is probably now back to normal but the fact that their Rotterdam plant was down for turnaround is a good part of the reason why U.S. prices here have been high. (That) means this shipment could ease values," said a U.S. trader.
Rotterdam ships about 270,000 barrels of MTBE to the U.S. Gulf and East Coasts every six weeks.
Also, MTBE shipments from Venezuela's Superoctanos plant are running about 10 days behind after production was back up at full capacity on Wednesday following a prolonged outage, traders said.

Another international products broker said more than 1.5 million barrels of gasoline was fixed earlier this week for a transatlantic voyage into the East Coast. The shipments were to be loading late July and early August.
